en.bestFor: Turning an idea, article or set of notes into a clear concept explainer for Reels, Shorts, marketing or presentations — any topic that is clearer as an explanation graph than as a character holding props.
en.structure: Each clip runs 3–8 seconds and the count follows the content: about 1–2 clips for a micro short, 2–4 for 15–20s, 4–6 for 30–45s, and 7–10 for a full 50–60s explainer.
en.hook: The first one to two seconds stack at least two hooks at once — a punchy spoken line plus a visual or sound opener, such as the character sliding into frame, an oversized prop popping up, or a sudden whoosh.
en.arc: Picks the pattern that suits the source, e.g. surprise → setup → how it works → consequence → takeaway for education, or pain point → reveal → proof → call to action for products. The main answer is held back until near the end, and the video finishes on a clean resting payoff rather than looping.
en.narrator: A warm adult male voice narrates every line from off-screen, in the third person. The character on screen stays silent and reacts to the diagram or props; the narrator may call it by name.
en.visual: A fixed whiteboard-doodle look: bold, slightly wobbly black lines with flat marker-style colour fills on a white canvas, starring a round-headed everyman (or your uploaded character). For every topic the canvas is an explanation graph — comparison, before/after, cause and effect, numbered steps, labeled parts, flow, or a simple chart — and the character can stand aside and react. Metaphor props (boxes, bins, arrows, tags) are a fallback, not a three-prop quota. Short beat titles and diagram labels sit on the canvas, and something on screen changes every couple of seconds.
en.audio: Background music follows the emotional turn of the script, with quick sound effects (pops, whooshes, dings) timed to visual changes. Narration is voice only; beat titles and diagram labels may sit on the canvas.
en.rules: You must pick an aspect ratio. The source's meaning is kept and no facts or figures are invented. For every topic, an explanation graph is the main subject. Density comes from the graph — never from a three-prop quota. Beat titles and diagram labels are allowed on canvas. The whiteboard style and character design stay locked — no chalkboard version or replacement hero. You approve the storyboard before any video is made.
